meta.title: What is autonoetic consciousness? Examining what underlies subjective experience in memory and future thinking
meta.domain: Cognitive psychology — autonoetic consciousness, episodic memory, mental time travel, psychometrics
meta.overview: Two studies (N=342) using factor analysis of subjective ratings to identify the latent markers of autonoetic consciousness across autobiographical memory, future simulation, and lab-encoded episodic memory. Re-experiencing and mental time travel emerge as core markers for memory; Remember/Know pools into a single strength factor; MTT drops out for future imagining; vivid first-person imagery underpins re-experiencing.
meta.abstract: Across two studies (N=342) with young healthy participants, exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis of subjective phenomenological ratings identified re-experiencing (and pre-experiencing for the future) plus mental time travel as core markers of autonoetic consciousness in memory. Remember and Know responses pooled into a single factor consistent with memory strength rather than distinct states of consciousness. Mental time travel did not load for imagining the future. The autonoetic factor structure predicted the richness of autobiographical narratives but not recall of a lab-encoded video, and vivid first-person visual imagery was associated with autonoetic re-experiencing.

claims.statement: Re-experiencing and mental time travel are the core markers of autonoetic consciousness in memory.
The Remember/Know paradigm indexes memory strength, not qualitatively distinct states of consciousness (R and K pool into one factor).
Mental time travel is not a core component of imagining future events (unlike memory).
Vivid, first-person visual imagery is associated with autonoetic re-experiencing of autobiographical memories.
The autonoetic factor structure predicts richness of autobiographical narratives (remote: F(3,199)=4.4, p=.005) but not recall of a lab-encoded video.

contributions.typing_rationale: Develops a data-driven framework identifying latent markers of autonoetic consciousness from subjective ratings across memory and future thinking.
Empirically ties specific mental-imagery features (vividness, first-person perspective) to autonoetic consciousness.
Provides evidence dissociating mental time travel from future simulation, favoring scene-construction over self-projection accounts for the future.
Challenges the Remember/Know paradigm as a proxy for qualitative subjective experience, reframing it as a strength index.

sota.resolver_notes: Undermind semantic search (year_max=2024) placed this among the remember/know + autonoetic-marker literature: Tulving 1985 (the construct operationalized), Irish 2008 (behavioural autonoetic-marker method), Wixted & Mickes 2010 (continuous dual-process R/K as strength — supports the strength reinterpretation), and Umanath & Coane 2020 (R/K face validity). Framework-level overlap; the data-driven factor structure of autonoetic markers is the novel contribution.
